assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly influential quantitative account of how distorted factor allocation across firms can generate large productivity and income gaps.
assessment.attribution: The proposed trio is a coherent credit group for the central measurement and development framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively used in research on productivity, development, and policy for many years.
uncertainties: The empirical magnitude and policy interpretation of measured misallocation remain debated.
Related work creates some difficulty in drawing a fully exclusive attribution boundary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and its empirical interpretation of trade gains and distributional effects.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplies the foundational model, with Helpman and Redding central to the broader theoretical and empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply embedded in trade research and has generated a large body of empirical evidence.
uncertainties: The breadth of subsequent contributors makes a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral-based propagation mechanisms provided a durable explanation for how financial conditions amplify macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are fundamental to collateral constraints, while Gertler is central to the financial-accelerator program.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have long been central to macro-finance theory and policy analysis, especially after financial crises.
uncertainties: The proposed discovery joins closely related but distinct models with partially overlapping credit claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work made political incentives, institutions, and state capacity central to rigorous analysis of fiscal policy and development.
assessment.attribution: The three scholars have made complementary, field-defining contributions to modern political economy.
assessment.maturity: The research has accumulated over decades and shaped both theoretical and empirical political economy.
uncertainties: The field is broad, so any compact laureate grouping leaves out other major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking structural analysis feasible across labour, industrial organization, and related fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust's foundational contribution is especially clearly identifiable; the other listed scholars made important extensions and applications.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been tested, extended, and routinely applied for several decades.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between the original framework and later computational and econometric advances is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification fundamentally changed how economists formulate credible conclusions when data and assumptions cannot point-identify parameters.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clearest foundational figure, with Tamer and Molinari important contributors to subsequent development.
assessment.maturity: The approach is a well-established part of econometric practice and has influenced empirical standards well beyond its original applications.
uncertainties: The cited contribution encompasses a broad methodological literature with many additional contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM gave applied researchers a practical, influential solution to pervasive endogeneity and persistence problems.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are the central names associated with the core estimator, with Blundell central to its major extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding workhorses in applied microeconometrics and macroeconomics.
uncertainties: Finite-sample weaknesses and instrument proliferation limit reliability in some applications.
Attribution between the core and system-GMM contributions requires a judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established that fairness, reciprocity, and inequity aversion are consequential for economic behavior and institutional design.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt supplied a canonical formalization, while Falk made major complementary experimental contributions.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been replicated, formalized, and incorporated into behavioural, labour, and organizational economics.
uncertainties: Experimental context and heterogeneity complicate claims about the universality of particular social-preference models.
